title: Use native CSR row occupancy in bounded relation probe
masterplan_authority: Revision 11 / Version 2.2.0 / Gate 1 — Renovation and owner-directed Genesis
finding: The 01CM diagnostic built strict Boolean CSR blocks correctly but queried them by iterating every stored entry twice, rebuilding two temporary source sets and sorting their intersection. That probe path ignored the already canonical shared row axis and CSR row offsets, so part of the observed CSR query cost measured harness reconstruction rather than the representation's native row-support operation.
primary_claim: The schema-v5 bounded relation probe now derives the strict Boolean CSR result directly from the exact shared row axis and row_offsets already present in TypedRelationBlock. A focused regression makes iter_entries() fail on this probe path. All comparison arms still must return the same deterministic result. This is a diagnostic/harness correction with zero production-code changes and introduces no query index, cache, backend, store, registry, graph authority, Tensor type, or semantic plane.
gardener_decision: Fix the already identified hot path in the existing diagnostic before considering any new optimization layer. Reuse row_axis.labels and row_offsets that TypedRelationBlock already owns, delete the diagnostic's two full entry rescans, two temporary source sets, and intersection sort, and pin that reuse with an adversarial monkeypatch regression. Do not add a second index or backend to compensate for a harness-level misuse of the existing CSR representation.

prior_01CM_hosted_observation.comparison_note: The large drop from the separate 01CM hosted observation to 01CN is evidence that the earlier diagnostic included avoidable entry-rescan/set/sort overhead. Because these are separate hosted runs, it is not used as a rigorous speedup or benchmark-superiority claim.

diagnostic_relation_probe.interpretation: Within the exact 01CN hosted run, strict Boolean CSR is much cheaper than generic TensorView for this row-support query but remains slower than direct Forest and far slower than the preindexed Forest baseline. This supports correcting the harness while retaining the negative architecture result: there is no evidence here for a new sparse backend or for promoting CSR as the general query engine.
